historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025), cross-checked against FY2026 guidance of high-single-digit revenue growth
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (19.0% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue (7.5%) and EPS (7.7%) 5yr CAGRs. Equity is NOT a usable growth anchor for Moody's: book equity was negative through FY2016-17 after years of buybacks and the FY2020 base (1,763) is depressed; ~3B/yr of repurchases keep it small relative to earnings. Revenue CAGR is the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2020->FY2025 and FY2022->FY2025, on fiscal-year (Dec) data. The 3-year figures all start from the FY2022 issuance trough (revenue -12%, reported FCF 1,191) and overstate trend; the 5-year figures bracket a full issuance cycle (2020-21 refinancing boom, 2022 bust, 2024-25 recovery) and are the ones used. Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC add-back - equity-award taxes (interest income 0, net-debt company): FY20 1,785; FY21 1,608; FY22 935; FY23 1,616; FY24 2,209; FY25 2,242; TTM Jun-26 2,609. Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (4.7%) equals the reported-FCF 5yr CAGR -- SBC has grown in line with cash flow, not faster (SBC+taxes 4.8% of revenue FY20, 4.3% FY25).

scenario_narratives.base: Moody's compounds revenue at ~7% for four years then decelerates to 3.5% by Y10: MA's >95%-recurring subscription base (45% of revenue) grows 8-9% on KYC, insurance/catastrophe and lending software plus AI-native products, while MIS grows mid-single-digit through the cycle as global issuance tracks nominal debt stock growth and private-credit ratings add a new leg. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin edges from 53.5% to 55%; SBC including withholding taxes stays ~4-4.4% of revenue; capex 4.5% carries bolt-on M&A; cash tax 23%. Discounted at 9% with 3% terminal growth, 20x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Issuance strength proves structural rather than an AI-capex artefact: leveraged-finance refinancing, hyperscaler and structured-finance volumes keep growing, rate cuts arrive, and private-credit ratings become a material MIS revenue line. The Microsoft Copilot / AWS / Anthropic distribution of Moody's data lifts MA to low-double-digit growth with operating leverage, taking pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 57%. Revenue grows 8.5-9.5% for four years.
scenario_narratives.bear: Rate cuts slip and a credit event in private credit or AI-datacenter financing shuts the issuance window: consolidated revenue falls 5% in Y2 (FY2022 was -12%), pre-SBC margin drops to 48.5% on fixed analyst cost, and recovery is slower because private credit keeps bypassing public ratings and regulators tighten scrutiny of ratings on novel structures. The business is re-rated as cyclical: 2.5% terminal growth and a 16x terminal cap. No solvency issue (interest cover ~15x) -- this is a multiple and margin reset, not distress.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF basis: SBC plus the cash withholding taxes on equity awards are expensed (4.4% of revenue, ~358 TTM) and the share count is held flat, so the ~3B/yr of buybacks are value-neutral rather than a source of per-share growth. No interest income is stripped because Moody's is a net-debt company (6,050). Flows are built from components -- pre-SBC EBITDA margin, SBC %, D&A, 23% cash tax on unlevered EBIT, capex incl. bolt-on M&A allowance, zero net working-capital capture -- rather than carrying the H1-26 peak FCF margin forward. The duopoly moat and regulatory barrier justify a 20x terminal cap and 3% terminal growth in base, but a 9% USD WACC is applied uniformly and the cyclicality is charged through a 25% bear weight, not through the discount rate. The street basis (SBC as non-cash) is reported alongside so the reader can see how much of the market price depends on the SBC convention.
key_risks_to_valuation: Issuance cyclicality: MIS transactional revenue can fall 20%+ in a credit-market shutdown (FY2022 consolidated revenue -12%); the bear path models one such year
A meaningful slice of 2025-26 issuance growth is AI-datacenter and hyperscaler financing; if that capex cycle cools, both volumes and ratings-quality reputational risk are exposed together
Private-credit disintermediation of public ratings may outrun Moody's private-credit ratings revenue
Terminal value is the majority of EV in every scenario; a 1pp change in WACC moves the base IV by roughly 15-20%
Net debt 6,050 and debt-funded buybacks: in a downturn capital return slows, and the flat-share-count convention then relies on SBC being expensed, which it is
Cash tax rate: FY25 cash taxes ran at 25% of EBIT; if Sec.174 relief does not lower it, each 1pp of tax costs ~1.3% of IV
FX: roughly half of revenue is non-USD; a stronger dollar reduces reported growth

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular-session close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 402.28-546.88
data_sources.financials: MCO_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL via build_facts_xbrl.py, 111 periods FY2006-Q2 2026) via metrics_normalized; kpis table for buybacks, equity-award taxes, D&A and cash taxes; FY2025 10-K and Q1/Q2-2026 10-Qs underlying. TTM base = FY2025 + H1-2026 - H1-2025.
data_sources.qualitative: MCO_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): business model, moat, risks, bull/bear, Q2-2026 results and FY2026 guidance (revenue high-single-digit growth, adj. EPS $16.50-17.00, FCF $2.7-2.9B, buybacks up to $3.0B, issuance mid-single-digit growth).

inputs.share_count_basis: 174.5m at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2-26 10-Q; Q2-26 net income 879 / diluted EPS 5.04 = 174.4m, so the period-end count and the diluted weighted average coincide to within 0.1m). Held FLAT: SBC incl. equity-award taxes is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. Buybacks (TTM 3,115) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30 Jun 2026: cash-flow-statement SBC add-back 233 (FY25 234 + H1-26 117 - H1-25 118) PLUS cash taxes paid on net-share settlement ~125 (FY25 99 + Q1-26 76 - H1-25 88, Q2-26 assumed at Q2-25's 35; Q2-26 figure not yet in the kpis table). Moody's publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure, so the two lines are summed per owner-fcf.md s1(a).
inputs.buyback_note: TTM financing-activity repurchases: FY25 1,607 + H1-26 2,165 - H1-25 657. FY26 guidance 'up to $3.0B'. Partly debt-funded: total debt rose 6,994 -> 7,517 between Dec-25 and Jun-26 while cash fell 2,384 -> 1,467.
inputs.fy0_note: Base year is the trailing twelve months to 30 Jun 2026 (FY2025 + H1-2026 - H1-2025) so the flow base shares a date with the net-debt and share-count anchors. Revenue 8,160; GAAP EBITDA (OI + D&A) 4,150; D&A 495; capex 352; OCF 3,319; reported FCF 2,967. Adjusted pre-SBC EBITDA = 4,150 + 233 = 4,383 (53.7% of revenue). Year 1 of the projection is the twelve months to Jun-2027.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Risk-free 4.1% (10y UST, Oct-2026), ERP 5.0%, beta 1.1 (5y monthly vs S&P ~1.1-1.25) -> cost of equity 9.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (A3/BBB+ senior notes), 3.8% after 21% tax. Debt/EV ~9% (7.5B debt vs ~78B market cap) -> WACC 9.1%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (~$0.4B ROU) are expensed inside operating income, so lease cost already sits inside the EBITDA margin; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. One treatment only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (<0.5% of net income); no adjustment.
inputs.tax_note: Cash tax rate on unlevered EBIT: FY25 cash taxes 825 / EBIT-after-equity-taxes 3,252 = 25%; FY24 22%; FY23 17%. The FY25 rate was inflated by Sec.174 R&D capitalisation, reversed by the 2025 OBBBA restoration of immediate expensing, so 23% is used as the run-rate (GAAP effective ~21-22%; the engine does not credit the interest tax shield inside the flows, it sits in the after-tax cost of debt).
inputs.working_capital_note: wc_capture 0 in all scenarios. Deferred revenue grows ~100-130/yr (15-20% of the revenue increase) but receivables grow with it and FY25/TTM OCF ran ~200-275 BELOW NI + D&A + SBC, so the net working-capital contribution is slightly negative to neutral. Calibration: TTM unlevered owner FCF from the components at 23% tax and zero WC is ~2,845; less ~235 after-tax interest = 2,610 vs actual levered owner FCF 2,609.
inputs.capex_note: Capex 4.3% of revenue TTM; set at 4.5% to carry a small allowance for the bolt-on data/analytics acquisitions (CAPE Analytics, Praedicat etc.) that replenish the acquired-intangible amortisation inside D&A. D&A 6.1% TTM (incl. ~2.5pp acquired-intangible amortisation) glides to 5.5% as older deals roll off.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (owner_fcf_dcf_component), 10-year horizon, probability-weighted bear/base/bull, house (SBC expensed) and street (SBC non-cash) bases. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: Moody's is a US operating company (ratings duopoly + recurring analytics software/data), has disclosed SBC, net DEBT (so no interest-income strip), no NCI, single currency -- the owner-FCF adaptations file does not apply. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). Price is a regular-session close, not after-hours. Net debt and share count are both from the Q2-2026 (30 Jun 2026) balance sheet; the Q3-2026 10-Q is due 21 Oct 2026 and should refresh both. The share count is held flat and buybacks are value-neutral because SBC incl. withholding taxes is fully expensed; the flat count IS being funded (TTM repurchases 3,115, 8.7x the SBC charge).

bear.narrative: A 2022-style issuance air pocket: H2-26 stalls as rate cuts slip, then a credit event (private-credit or AI-datacenter-debt stress) cuts MIS transactional revenue sharply in Y2 (consolidated -5%, versus -12% in FY2022) while MA keeps growing. Margins compress to 48.5% pre-SBC on fixed analyst costs and recover only to 52%. Private credit disintermediates more public issuance than it adds in ratings, and regulatory scrutiny of private-credit ratings raises compliance cost. Lower terminal growth (2.5%) and a 16x cap for a business whose cyclicality has been re-rated.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 (TTM to Jun-27) 6.5%: FY26 guidance is high-single-digit growth over FY25 (7,718 -> ~8,370-8,400), and with H1-26 already +11.6% that implies H2-26 of only ~+5%; rolling that H2 plus a ~7% H1-27 forward against the 8,160 TTM base gives ~6.5%. Y2-Y4 7%: MA recurring revenue (45% of the mix, >95% subscription) compounding ~8-9% plus MIS mid-single-digit through-cycle issuance growth with private-credit ratings as the incremental leg. Decelerates 0.5pp/yr from Y5 to 3.5% in Y10 ahead of 3.0% terminal growth.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA margin was 53.7% TTM, 52.6% FY25, 54.7% H1-26. Y1 starts at 53.5%, a touch below TTM because H2-26 issuance is guided to slow, then adds ~15bp/yr to 55% as MA margins climb toward management's mid-30s target and MIS operating leverage holds; no credit for the H1-26 peak persisting.

bull.narrative: Issuance stays strong (AI-datacenter/hyperscaler and leveraged-finance refinancing waves continue, rate cuts arrive), private-credit ratings scale into a multi-hundred-million revenue line, and the Copilot/AWS/Claude AI distribution lifts MA growth to low-double-digits with margins expanding toward 57% pre-SBC. Tax at 22% reflects the lower end of the effective-rate range.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because MIS (55% of revenue) is issuance-cyclical and an issuance bust has occurred within the last four years (FY2022: revenue -12%, owner FCF -42%); management itself flagged a volatile rate-cut path as the H2-26 swing factor. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once -- sustained AI-linked issuance, rate cuts, private-credit ratings scaling AND AI monetisation in MA -- and the balance sheet is now net debt ~6B after debt-funded buybacks, so there is no net-cash cushion that would justify a heavier bull weight. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
